PullRequest.Title: agentHost: explain SSH servers that only offer host certificates and classify SSH connect failures
PullRequest.Body:

Refs #325647

The Agents window connects over SSH with `ssh2`, which cannot negotiate OpenSSH host certificates (`*-cert-v01@openssh.com`). This PR explains that failure and makes `vscodeAgents.sshConnect/attempt` able to tell it apart, along with other failure causes and automatic attempts.

## Explain servers that only offer host certificates

A server whose `HostKeyAlgorithms` only allows certificates fails key exchange with the bare `Handshake failed: no matching host key format`. The connection error (notification, connection hover and log) now continues:

> The server only offers host key types that are not supported here, such as OpenSSH host certificates. To connect, the server also needs to offer a plain host key, for example by adding ssh-ed25519 to HostKeyAlgorithms in its sshd_config.

Servers that configure `HostCertificate` without restricting `HostKeyAlgorithms` already work: they offer the plain key too, `ssh2` negotiates it, and the existing "configured to use a certificate authority" host key prompt applies. ProxyJump is not a workaround for a certificate-only target, because `ssh2` still performs the target's key exchange over the `ssh -W` stream.

## Classify SSH connect failures and report automatic attempts

The event classified failures by matching English message text in the renderer. Remote command output such as `Permission denied` during CLI installation counted as `authentication`, and every handshake failure counted as `other`. It was also only sent from a few user-initiated code paths.

- The shared process records a failure code with the stage that failed (`config`, `ssh`, `cliInstall`, `agentHost`, `relay`) and, for the SSH handshake, why (`hostKeyFormat`, `kexAlgorithm`, other `handshake` failure, `network`). Shared-process IPC only carries an error's name, message and stack, so the code travels in the name of generic errors and the renderer's SSH factory restores the name. Errors identified by name (host key denial, SSH authentication, cancellation) are unchanged.
- The event gets a `stage` field (`protocol` for the Agent Host protocol handshake) and the `hostKeyFormat`, `kexAlgorithm` and `handshake` categories. Authentication is identified by error name instead of message text. Boolean fields are classified as measurements.
- `RemoteAgentHostService` reports each dial's outcome to its connection factory through a new optional `reportConnectionAttempt`, after deciding whether to retry. The SSH factory sends the event for every attempt: explicit, on demand, at startup and automatic retries. `userInitiated` now tells automatic attempts apart. `attempt` numbers dials within a retry cycle, starting again at one when an established connection drops, and `willRetry` tells whether another attempt follows. The Agents window call sites that sent the event are removed to avoid counting attempts twice.

Not covered: relay recovery inside a live connection, which doesn't go through the factory, and proxy-specific categories.

## How to test

Run an `sshd` (OpenSSH 10.3p1 in Docker was used here) with a host certificate:

```
HostKey /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key
HostCertificate /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub
HostKeyAlgorithms ssh-ed25519-cert-v01@openssh.com
```

1. Connect to it from the Agents window (New > Remote > SSH): the error explains the limitation, and `vscodeAgents.sshConnect/attempt` reports `errorCategory: hostKeyFormat` and `stage: ssh` (set the Telemetry output channel's log level to Trace to see it).
2. Remove the `HostKeyAlgorithms` line: the host key prompt says that the host uses a certificate authority, and the connection succeeds after confirming.
3. With a saved host, stop the server and reload the window: automatic attempts report `userInitiated: false` and an increasing `attempt`.

## Validation

`pnpm install` fails locally on `main` (an internal-feed dependency is missing), so the dependencies come from an install at 699a5b3c877. The client was transpiled from this branch with `node build/next/index.ts transpile`, after linking two build packages from the local store, and the tests ran against that output.

- `scripts\test.bat --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/common/sshConnectTelemetry.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/sshRemoteAgentHostService.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/electron-browser/sshRemoteAgentHostService.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/electron-browser/remoteAgentHostService.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/sshAgentHost.contribution.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/remoteAgentHostActions.test.ts`: passed (356 passing, 1 pending).
- The new "numbers dials per retry cycle" test fails with dials numbered from the retry budget (0 passing, 1 failing), and the "explains a server that only offers host certificates" case fails with the message change reverted.
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed (0 errors).
- `pnpm run oxlint` on the changed files: passed.
- Manual, for the message: the built `SSHRemoteAgentHostMainService._connectSSH` with the real `ssh2` against a Docker `sshd`. A certificate-only server is rejected with the new message. A server with `HostCertificate` and default `HostKeyAlgorithms`, with an `@cert-authority` `known_hosts` entry, gets the `ca-only` host key prompt and connects.

Scenarios.Scenario: Explicit or on-demand SSH connection, including first-time CLI installation and endpoint selection
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The caller waits for the renderer factory's shared-process connect/reconnect request, SSH configuration and authentication, CLI availability, endpoint selection/startup, relay acquisition, and Agent Host protocol initialization. Reporting runs after resolving/rejecting connection waiters; telemetry transport completion is not awaited.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke the shared-process SSH connect or reconnect service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per actual renderer dial, not per joining caller; renderer pending-connection maps coalesce requests for the same address.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same connect/reconnect request and coalescing existed before the diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run ssh -G and, when configured, launch an SSH jump helper or ProxyCommand.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one ssh -G per new physical session; the resolved object is passed onward. Optional proxy creation occurs once per new physical session, not per endpoint. Existing sessions bypass configuration/session bootstrap.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical calls and placement; the diff wraps existing promises to tag errors without repeating operations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Configuration resolution and proxy setup precede the SSH handshake.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read authentication keys and configured known_hosts files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Agent authentication reads up to five default key paths and an optional nondefault explicit path; key-file authentication reads its explicit file. Trust evidence reads the configured known_hosts paths. These occur per new session as before.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same file reads existed; error-code annotations add no reads or retries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Key preparation and host verification precede completed authentication.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Establish SSH, execute remote platform/CLI checks, optionally download/install the CLI, discover endpoints, and start an agent if needed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One physical SSH connection per distinct uncached connection key; two uname calls; existing CLI checks; one initial endpoint-list command plus one concurrent liveness command per distinct PID, not per registry entry. Starting an agent adds one spawn and bounded sequential registry polling. None of these counts change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The complete bootstrap and all its remote commands/download behavior already existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: CLI readiness and endpoint selection are awaited before relay acquisition; agent spawn is fire-and-forget but registration polling is awaited.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire a logical relay using one SSH forwardOut channel or one agent-relay exec channel, then initialize the protocol.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One relay per logical client; pending replacement acquisitions join by expected connection ID. Multiple renderers can share a physical SSH session while retaining separate relay leases.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same session reuse, lease grouping, relay boundary, and protocol initialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before the connection becomes usable.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Submit one bounded connection-outcome telemetry record to the shared-process appender when telemetry is enabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One event per completed nondiscarded factory dial, not per endpoint or joining caller. Previously instrumented explicit UI paths also emitted one event; their old calls are removed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Outcome reporting was at selected UI call sites; this moves ownership to the factory rather than adding duplicate reports on those paths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Small synchronous classification/sanitization and IPC enqueue; completion of IPC or telemetry delivery is not awaited.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct SSH addresses, concurrent logical clients, distinct remote endpoint PIDs, configured trust files, and cold installation/agent-start state.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One renderer dial per address; shared physical-session bootstrap is coalesced by key. Independent hosts may proceed concurrently, and endpoint liveness probes run concurrently per distinct PID. Per-session bootstrap stages and registry polling remain ordered. No new concurrency is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Renderer pending maps join same-address callers. Shared-process _pendingSessions joins bootstrap by connection key and _connections reuses successful sessions. Installed commit-keyed CLIs are reused; misses install/download using the existing helper. A renderer with an already usable connection returns its handle without a new factory dial. Failure-code wrappers do not change positive or negative cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced both renderer coalescing and shared-process session/relay ownership, plus the remote command, subprocess, filesystem, and telemetry enqueue implementations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No timing measurements; host latency, key/trust-file sizes, endpoint counts, and cold CLI installation prevalence vary.
Scenarios.Verdict: No actionable performance regression: expensive bootstrap boundaries, grouping, and ordering are unchanged. Added error annotations and bounded outcome metadata do not amplify existing bootstrap work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Startup autoconnection to saved SSH hosts and automatic retries of unavailable hosts
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each configured host independently waits for its existing connect pipeline. A failed attempt schedules the next existing backoff before reporting its outcome; telemetry delivery does not gate the next retry.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dial configured hosts through the shared-process SSH service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One dial per distinct configured address that is not already connected or pending. A default retry cycle has at most ten scheduled retries after an initial failed dial; terminal authentication/cancellation cases stop as before.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same saved-host dials, terminal-error checks, pending joins, backoff, and retry budget existed. The new _dialAttempts counter is separate from the existing retry-budget map.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Hosts are unavailable until their own connection attempt succeeds; backoff remains 1 second initially with a 30-second ceiling.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve configuration and create a physical SSH session only when no reusable or pending session exists.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One configuration-resolution subprocess per uncached physical-session attempt; successful or pending sessions are reused by key. Failed sessions may be retried under the existing budget.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same subprocess issuance and session cache behavior; withSSHConnectFailureCode observes the already-created promise.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Configuration and SSH transport establishment gate that host's dial.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Record automatic connection outcomes through the existing telemetry appender.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One bounded event per nondiscarded actual dial, therefore proportional to unique hosts times existing attempts, not to caller count, endpoints, or progress updates. Disabled telemetry avoids appender calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Automatic startup/retry outcomes generally were not recorded at the removed UI telemetry sites.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Delivery is asynchronous and unawaited; the retry decision and timer are established first.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of distinct saved hosts and actual failed dials within the unchanged retry cycle; separate windows may each own a logical dial but physical-session bootstrap is shared by connection key.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Independent addresses may dial concurrently as before, with no global limiter introduced or removed. Each address retains one in-flight dial and one reconnect timer. Reporting does not issue another dial or await network telemetry.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: In-flight attempts are joined per address and per physical connection key; successful sessions are reused. Failed attempts retain the existing retry policy rather than adding a negative cache. Telemetry's pre-experiment buffer is bounded by the existing MAX_BUFFER_SIZE.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: compared the old and new short-circuit retry expressions, the separate counter maps, and telemetry's gating/buffering/IPC implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Unknown typical saved-host count and telemetry enqueue duration; no evidence of a high-frequency unbounded telemetry loop added by this change.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Automatic attempts gain intentionally bounded instrumentation, while connection concurrency and the expensive retry workload remain unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Recovery of an established SSH connection, including relay-only recovery and protocol-handshake failure
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing protocol client first attempts self-recovery. Fatal outer recovery rebuilds through the factory; protocol incompatibility and terminal authentication failures stop retries. New telemetry describes these decisions without waiting for delivery.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request relay/session reconnection using the current connection ID.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per existing inner recovery attempt; shared-process pending reconnects coalesce replacement requests for the same expected connection ID.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same reconnect request, parameters, lease reuse, and recovery ordering existed; the added catch only decodes error metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Relay recovery must finish before the live protocol client can resume.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reuse the current SSH session to open a replacement relay, or perform the existing cold bootstrap if the physical session is gone. A non-timeout relay failure may reread endpoint discovery once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One replacement relay per effective acquisition after expected-ID coalescing; endpoint reread occurs once on the existing applicable failure path, not once per endpoint. Full bootstrap is avoided for a reusable session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same relay creation, failure reread, cleanup, and retry behavior. The replacement thrown error now carries a stage code but performs no extra command.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited by inner recovery; outer recovery uses existing backoff after failure.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enqueue an outcome record for an outer factory dial.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One event per nondiscarded factory dial; ongoing inner relay recovery does not invoke this factory reporting hook. Interrupted initial protocol handshakes report once with willRetry, rather than reporting every subsequent live transport event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only selected explicit reconnect UI paths emitted this outcome event; those emissions are removed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Outcome reporting follows the retry decision; delivery is not awaited.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Actual transport drops, outer retry cycles, logical relay clients, and independent connection IDs; not session-history length or message traffic.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The existing inner recovery client retains ownership until terminal failure; the outer service does not rebuild during self-healing reconnect. Pending outer dials join per address; pending relay replacements join per expected connection ID.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing SSH sessions and pending relay replacements are reused. Successful recovery resets both the old retry-budget map and new dial-number map. Inner reconnects do not generate additional factory-operation map entries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced self-healing versus fatal recovery branches, shared-process lease acquisition, unchanged boundary calls, and all report-hook call sites.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Drop frequency and transport-recovery duration are environment-dependent; no measurements were available.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence performance regression. Error classification does not alter recovery scheduling or increase the number of SSH/relay operations.

Scenarios.Scenario: Connection removal, disposal, and generic non-SSH connection bookkeeping
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing removal/disposal paths cancel reconnect timers and dispose clients/transports. Generic non-SSH dials execute their existing factories and handshake; only SSH implements the new optional production reporting hook.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run existing transport/client disposal while clearing per-address retry bookkeeping.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing disposal work remains once per removed connection/transport generation. The diff adds scalar counter deletion or map clearing, not additional transport disposal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same clients, transports, and timers were removed; only the new dial-number map needs additional bookkeeping.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Same synchronous teardown placement as before.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Active or failed addresses, removed connections, and actual dial count. New maps hold address keys and scalar operation/count values, not SSH clients, errors, payloads, or connection histories.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No changes to disposal ordering, pending-dial identity guards, or factory invocation concurrency. Repository search confirms no other production factory implements reportConnectionAttempt.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Dial counters are reset on successful/incompatible connections, explicit fresh reconnect, removal, disablement, and service disposal. Normal SSH outcome reporting deletes the per-dial operation entry. No new heavyweight cache or eager factory construction is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for unchanged resource ownership and optional-hook reachability; no substantial diff-introduced retention mechanism established.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Rare discarded attempts can leave small scalar factory bookkeeping until replacement/factory lifetime ends; inspected paths do not establish significant retained-resource growth under a realistic high-volume workflow.
Scenarios.Verdict: No actionable performance finding. Generic connection paths gain constant-size bookkeeping without new subprocess, network, filesystem, or database calls.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across all 14 changed files and every diff page, including added/changed tests. Traced explicit connection, cold/warm bootstrap, saved-host startup/retries, live relay recovery, telemetry IPC, and cleanup ownership. No high-confidence actionable performance regressions or concrete performance-regression fixes were established. Static read-only review; magnitude was not profiled.
